context_for_the_survey_run.basis: geometry tests against published maps; nothing is attached to the record

limits: the reference is a published map compiled from topographic maps, not a field survey; its outlines may be offset by as much as 100 m
a mapped sinkhole counted as found means a closed basin of at least the stated depth lies where the map puts it; it is a shape, not an opening or an identity
the displaced control shows how often agreement arises by chance in ground this full of hollows
the detector reports the outermost closed basin; a sinkhole nested inside a larger closed depression is not reported as its own object
precision is not stated, because the map lists only sinkholes deeper than 30 m
one tile of one karst terrain was compared; the result does not transfer to other ground or to the seabed
no threshold was changed and no registry record was changed by this run

method.match_rule: a mapped outline is found when a detected basin's centroid lies within the outline's equivalent radius plus the publisher's positional offset; one-to-one, nearest first

reference_sets.crs_basis: The export declares no coordinate reference system and holds projected metres. The parent database holds the definition NAD_1983_StatePlane_Puerto_Rico_Virgin_Islands_FIPS_5200 and records a projection step dated 2012; its descriptive metadata still names a polyconic projection, which the coordinates cannot be (they are positive and offset by 200,000 m). Coherence check: bound to EPSG:32161, 1,171 of 1,173 outlines fall inside the independently published northern karst limit.
reference_sets.positional_basis: Publisher's metadata: "Offsets of as much as 100 meters between the karst data and base map topographic features may occur." The outlines were digitised from scanned paper maps at 1:20,000 and 1:140,000; the source map has a 50 m contour interval.
reference_sets.publisher_statement: Polygons showing locations of sinkholes deeper than 30 meters in Puerto Rico.

reference_sets.crs_basis: Same parent database and same basis as usgs_karst_sinkholes_over_30m.
reference_sets.publisher_statement: Polygons showing areas of sinkholes 5-30 meters deep in Puerto Rico. These are areas, not individual sinkholes.

reference_sets.crs_basis: The projection file inside the archive names EPSG:6566.
reference_sets.publisher_statement: Northern karst topography. This dataset extends from Rincon (northwest) to Rio Grande (northeast) municipalities. Source: PR Planning Board, 2010.

2018.evaluation_statement: compared with a published map: agreement with another interpretation, not field-verified accuracy
2018.precision_note: not stated: the map lists only features deeper than its stated depth, so a shallower basin it does not list is not an error

surface_agreement.measure: deepest fill depth below spill level inside each mapped outline
